natalie: Heads-up — trying to bring up AstraLite-v1 (Mistral fork) into the Gemma serving pipeline. Quick int4 smoke shows a clear quality drop on our summarization evals. Posting logs and initial numbers. :frowning:
omar: Can you paste the exact convert command you used? suspect rotary/headmap mismatch.
lee: if it's a Mistral->Gemma conversion there are known head-order + rotary scaling differences, could be head-concat vs split.
sasha: copying the log excerpt from the converter:
```
$ python tools/convert_model.py --src mistral --dst gemma --model astralite-v1 \n  --vocab-map mappings/astralite_vocab.json --quant int4 --rotary-mode auto
[INFO] export: rotary_head_dim=60, gemma-expected=64
[WARN] rotary-handshake: head_dim mismatch -> applying truncation
[WARN] quant: int4 per-tensor calibration applied
```
omar: that truncation line is the red flag. truncating head dim silently will change rotation frequency and break positional alignment. :eyes:
maria: quick eval snapshot (summarize-suite, rouge-l):
- gemma-fp16 (baseline): 0.412
- gemma-int8 (converted): 0.405
- gemma-int4 (converted): 0.287  <-- big drop
lee: float16 vs int4 gap like that screams rotary phase aliasing or token id remap. try running the token-id alignment tool: `tools/tokenmap_check.py --src vocab/astralite.json --dst vocab/gemma.json`
natalie: ran tokenmap_check, output shows 3 sentinel aliases and a shifted BOS index. also found KV-cache offset mismatch in a few examples.
sasha: quick patch idea: instead of truncating, do per-head interpolation to map 60->64 and scale the rotary angles accordingly. prototype command:
```
$ python tools/convert_model.py --rotary-resample head_interp --interp-method linear \n  --rotary-target-dim 64 --headmap even_split
```
omar: ran the interp patch on 10 evals. results improved: int4 -> rouge-l 0.34 (was 0.287), still below baseline but much closer.
maria: can you attach one failing example (input + reference + outputs) so we can see token-level divergence?
lee: also try switching quant backend to per-channel vs per-tensor; int4 per-channel sometimes preserves distribution and avoids phase drift. command:
`python quant/bench.py --backend per-channel --bits 4 --model astra-converted`
ci-bot: Build #4721 finished: conversion e2e job -> https://ci.redwood.example/builds/4721 (artifacts: models/astralite/conv-interp-64-int4.tar.gz) :white_check_mark:
natalie: attached failing case (pasted below) — small difference at token 8 causes prefix to drift after rotary wrap.
---
INPUT: "Summarize the product meeting notes for Q1"
REF: "Key takeaways: roadmap, hiring, budget cuts"
GEMMA-int4-output: "Key update: roadmap and budget"
GEMMA-fp16-output: "Key takeaways: roadmap, hiring, budget cuts"
---
omar: that aligns with subtle phase mis-align on early tokens. propose 3-step plan: 1) run full eval with interp mapping + per-channel int4, 2) add tokenmap assertions to converter (fail instead of truncating), 3) smoke test KV-cache replay on long-context examples.
sasha: added a small assertion patch to the converter; PR #1289. If tokenmap mismatch -> fail with context dump.
maria: I'll run the full eval overnight on dedicated infra (queue id D-908). Will report numbers in morning. :coffee:
lee: one more thought — Gemma runtime applies a headwise rotary scale factor (sqrt(2) on some exports). try adding `--rotary-scale-factor 1.4142` to conversion as an experiment.
natalie: thanks all. leaving this thread open — assigning follow-up ticket INF-3421 to triage remaining gap. tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :memo:
